paragraphs.source_en: Three years before the death of the Fifth Dalai Lama, Sangye Gyatso assumed the office of Desi and held much arbitrary power over political affairs. After the Fifth Dalai Lama died, Kangxi further issued an imperial edict appointing him king of Tubo. Yet Lhazang Khan, who had inherited the khanship of the Mongol Khoshut tribe stationed in Qinghai, exercised a guardianship over Tibet; the contradictions arising from the two sides’ political checks upon one another grew ever sharper.

paragraphs.source_en: After the Fifth Dalai Lama passed away, the then-regent Tibetan king Sangye Gyatso and Lhazang Khan of the Khoshut Mongols struggled for power, keeping both the death of the Fifth Dalai Lama and the establishment of the Sixth Dalai Lama secret. The young Tsangyang Gyatso, for his part, was content to remain at home, a little immortal of his own making. In 1696, the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi’s reign, Kangxi personally led an expedition and put down the rebellion of the Dzungar Mongols. Awed by the power of the Qing court, the Tibetan king submitted a secret memorial to Kangxi in 1697, the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi: “The secret memorial of next year stated that, to the misfortune of all beings, the Fifth Dalai Lama passed away in the year renxu (1682, the yang water dog year), and his reincarnated pure body is now fifteen years old... Because at that time Tubo was at war with Ladakh, and fearing unrest among the Tangut (Tibetan) people, the mourning was kept secret...” The following year the Tibetan king welcomed Tsangyang Gyatso to the Potala Palace for the enthronement ceremony; when Tsangyang Gyatso formally became the Sixth Dalai Lama, he was already a handsome fifteen-year-old youth in the midst of passionate love. Tsangyang Gyatso took the Fifth Panchen Lama as his teacher, shaved his head, and received the vows.

paragraphs.source_en: The Khoshut kingdom of Qinghai and Qaidam, and its protectorate in Tibet, appeared from Güshi Khan to his great-grandson Lhazang Khan (1700-1717) in the role of protectors of the Yellow Sect. Lhazang Khan zealously presided over the religious rites for selecting incarnate lamas and intervened in Tibet against the ministers who held real power. Lhazang Khan attacked Sangye Gyatso for “using a young Dalai Lama as a talisman to hold the political power of the Yellow Sect.” Tsangyang Gyatso, who had no wish to become the Dalai Lama, was publicly proclaimed the reincarnated soul-child of the Fifth Dalai Lama at the same time that news of the Fifth Dalai Lama’s death was made public. Thinking of it now, how inconceivable it is: the death of one life and the birth of another were originally only a year apart, yet this secret succession actually stretched across a long fifteen years.

paragraphs.source_en: That Tsangyang Gyatso was thrust onto the stormy crest of politics was likewise not something the Tibetan king Sangye Gyatso willingly chose; after the Tibetan king’s envoy submitted the secret memorial to Kangxi, he announced on his way back from the capital to Tibet that the Sixth Dalai Lama had grown weary of the world. Then Kangxi, “because the Desi (the Tibetan king) had from beginning to end shifted back and forth and held to both sides, summoned back his envoy and assembled the Mongols to proclaim the sealed secret document.” The Tibetan king fell into a political predicament, and Tsangyang Gyatso’s own situation can be imagined all the more. According to Research on Tsangyang Gyatso and His Love Songs published by Tibet People’s Publishing House, folk materials, and my own interviews, Tsangyang Gyatso was unwilling to assume the position of the Sixth Dalai Lama partly because he was deeply immersed in passionate love; and partly because by nature he was a person indifferent to fame and gain, lofty in aspiration, and “above the dust of the ordinary,” no matter how much he once wished to sink into the common world.

paragraphs.source_en: Under the strict supervision of the Tibetan king Sangye Gyatso, Tsangyang Gyatso began his study of the scriptures. Accustomed to a free life, Tsangyang Gyatso, though his heart and entrails burned from lost love, still could not sit still, and from time to time grew weary of study and went out walking. His scripture teachers followed after him and begged him to sit down and hear the teachings, fearing that Sangye Gyatso would hold them responsible; Tsangyang Gyatso often shed sorrowful tears over this anxious and uneasy way of studying, both for the teachers and for himself, and would pound his own head and beat his chest with his fists: “I truly never imagined that all the highs and lows, nobility and lowliness, joy and sorrow of human life would be gathered upon my head alone.” Seeing that, as long as he was willing to sit down and listen to the scriptures, the teachers would kowtow and bow, wholly forgetting that their own hair was white and grizzled, made Tsangyang Gyatso sigh with endless feeling. Tsangyang Gyatso was forced not only to study many scriptures, but also logic, poetry, and calendrical calculation. In addition, in winter Tsangyang Gyatso performed various vajra dances on the snow, and it is said that he was also trained to become a skilled archer.

paragraphs.source_zh: 仓央嘉措在藏王桑杰嘉措的严格监督下开始了学经。自由生活惯了的仓央嘉措，虽然因失恋五内俱焚可是仍坐不下来，时时厌学出去散步。经师们尾追恳请他坐下听经，唯恐桑杰嘉措追究责任，仓央嘉措往往为经师及自己这种心惊不安的学经方式而凄然泪下，常常用拳头猛击自己的头擂自己的胸：“真没想到，人世间的高低贵贱，欢乐悲伤全都集中到我一个人的头上。”看到自己只要肯坐下听经，经师们便又是叩头又是作揖，全然忘记了自己白发苍染更是令仓央嘉措感叹不已。仓央嘉措不仅被迫学了众多的经典还学了因明、诗歌和历算。此外在冬季仓央嘉措还在雪地上跳各种金刚舞，据说他还被训练成一个射箭能手。

paragraphs.source_en: As contradictions among Tibet’s upper ruling class grew ever sharper, the Tibetan king Sangye Gyatso, in order to achieve his aim of usurping power and monopolizing government, prevented Tsangyang Gyatso from involving himself in political affairs, launched great construction works, built anew the Zhaohou Dragon Palace pleasure garden, encouraged Tsangyang Gyatso to seek flowers and hunt beauty, and opened the way wide for his unrestrained conduct. In this way, Tsangyang Gyatso, sunk in the pain of lost love, became like a wild horse released back to the open, once started and impossible to rein in.

paragraphs.source_zh: 随着西藏上层统治阶级之间矛盾日益尖锐，藏王桑杰嘉措为了达到其窃权揽政的目的，不让仓央嘉措过问政事，并大兴土木，新建寨后龙宫游苑，怂恿仓央嘉措寻芳猎艳，并为仓央嘉措放荡不羁大开方便之门。就这样，沉溺于失恋痛苦之中的仓央嘉措如一头放归的野马一发而不可收。

paragraphs.source_en: Was it not so? The dream of first love was shattered, and all the primal desires of life quietly revived; the temple of love collapsed, and the venomous snakes and fierce beasts within life began to stir restlessly. Only then did Tsangyang Gyatso realize that what he found most unbearable about entering the Potala Palace was the Gelug school’s prohibition against monks marrying or approaching women. Deep palace compounds could hardly lock away the restless impulses of youth. Moreover, he was dignified in appearance, handsome and graceful, romantic and full of feeling, and far too many women adored him and gave him their hearts. Tsangyang Gyatso could no longer silently observe the pure rules and strict commandments of extreme asceticism. And the empty mystery of religion, together with the empty mystery of love, made him want to break free of these things and grasp at something real, however slight.

paragraphs.source_zh: 可不是？初恋的梦破灭，生命中各种原始的欲望悄然复活；爱情圣殿的坍塌，生命中的毒蛇猛兽蠢蠢欲动。仓央嘉措这才意识到入主布达拉宫最让自己受不了的是格鲁派佛教禁僧侣结婚，接近女性。深宫大院，难锁青春欲动。加上他相貌堂堂，英俊潇洒，风流多情，有太多的女子崇拜于他钟情于他。对极端禁欲主义的清规戒律仓央嘉措再也难以默守。而宗教的虚无神秘，加上爱情的虚无神秘都使他想挣脱这些，抓住一点现实的什么。

paragraphs.source_en: From then on, Tsangyang Gyatso plunged even more deeply into wine and women, gave free rein to his body, and sank into sensual desire. At times he even caused open and unrestrained uproars, going so far as to ignore repeated warnings from Emperor Kangxi, Lhazang Khan, and the Mongol princes. Tsangyang Gyatso would rather give up the honored rank of Dalai Lama than yield to emperors, kings, or princes, and he did so in order to sing the truest and purest love songs in his heart.
